title: Lark chat memory watermarks and NAS long-term archive
scope: Feishu/Lark assistant conversations must separate prompt context from local long-term memory storage.

acceptance_criteria.description: Short-term memory has an explicit token budget by Lark chat scenario; exceeding the budget produces a compress-or-trim action instead of passing full history to the LLM.
Medium-term memory has an explicit item/token watermark; exceeding it produces cleanup and promotion-candidate actions, not prompt expansion.
Long-term Lark chat records archive to NAS-style Chinese department/employee folders under knowledge/Chat/Lark Chat.
Long-term memory entry is represented as archive + index/distillation handoff, so full archives are never treated as LLM prompt context.

long_term.purpose: Local company memory and audit archive

non_goals: Do not use NAS archive size as prompt context size.
Do not send the full employee chat archive to the LLM by default.
Do not rely on manual /reset or /new as the only cost-control mechanism.
